request: Make a 90-second animated video about sleep

claims.text: Sleep is an active process during which the brain sorts memories and clears waste built up during the day.
The night is split into repeating cycles of light sleep, deep sleep and dream sleep, each doing different work for the body.
Going without enough sleep makes it harder to concentrate, remember new facts and react quickly to what happens around you.
Over months and years, regular short sleep is linked with higher risks of heart problems and weight gain.
Keeping the same bedtime and wake-up time, even on weekends, helps the body clock settle into a steady rhythm.
Bright screens late in the evening can delay sleepiness because light tells the brain that it is still daytime.
A cool, dark and quiet bedroom makes it easier to fall asleep and to stay asleep through the night.
Caffeine blocks the signals that build up sleep pressure, so a late coffee can keep you awake for hours.
While you sleep, hormones that support growth and repair are released, which is why rest matters after hard physical effort.
To build a better routine, first fix your wake-up time, then dim the lights early, and finally keep screens out of bed.
Sleep problems that last for weeks, such as loud snoring with daytime exhaustion, are worth discussing with a doctor.
Think of sleep like charging a phone overnight: skip it and you start the day running on a low battery.
